newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes gain more ground on Cano shutdown.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes gain more ground on Cano shutdown.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes gained further ground Tuesday afternoon after Occidental Petroleum declared force majeure on its Cano Limon field in Colombia, traders said.
Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol has had force majeure on loadings in place since July 6 after a string of rebel attacks on the 250,000 barrel per day (bpd) Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline.

Oxy's move on Tuesday, however, was the first time ever that the company declared force majeure on the 180,000 bpd field. The action frees the firm from its obligations to employees and contractors on the site.
At least two U.s. refiners, Amoco and Exxon, have been looking for alternative crude to make up for delays on their Cano loadings.

August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was running around $19.65-75 a barrel on Tuesday afternoon, about two to three cents ahead of the futures price, factoring in the current exchange-for-physical premium, traders said.
Sour grades were most affected by the Cano developments, although sweets were also getting a lift.
"It's Cano that's affecting sours, the rest of the stuff is just hitching a ride," a Gulf Coast trader said.
West Texas Sour/Midland last traded at WTI minus $1.10 a barrel, up from $1.20 discount this morning.
Eugene Island changed hands at minus $1.30 a barrel, up a nickel from this morning.
Among sweet grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James last moved at plus 25 cents, up five cents from earlier today.
WTI/Midland was done at minus 25 cents, up one cent from this morning and two cents from Monday.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/St. James was placed at minus 30 cents, up slightly from recent talk.
Finally, WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was last traded at $1.88 a barrel, up from $1.85 this morning.
